A.explanation: The geometrical centre equals the centre of gravity only for a uniform symmetrical object, not for irregular or non-uniform objects.

B.explanation: This is the syllabus definition: the whole weight $W$ can be treated as a single force acting at the centre of gravity for moments and equilibrium.

C.explanation: Zero net torque depends on all applied forces and the chosen pivot, not only on weight, and the centre of gravity can lie outside the object.

D.explanation: Gravity acts on every particle of the object throughout its volume, not at one single point where gravity acts.

hints: Notice the four options use different ideas: geometrical centre, weight considered to act, zero net torque, and where gravity acts.
Recall that weight is distributed over the whole object but for calculating moments you replace it by one single force $W$ at one point.
Check which wording matches the standard definition and why the geometrical centre and the zero-torque point fail for irregular objects.
walkthrough: Identify the use of centre of gravity: it simplifies the distributed weight of an extended object into one force for moments and balance.
State the physical rule: the centre of gravity is defined as the point at which the weight of the object may be considered to act.
Test the distractors: option A is true only for uniform regular shapes, option D is wrong because gravity pulls on all mass, and option C is wrong because net torque involves all forces and pivots.
Matching the definition to the list gives a single exact statement about weight considered to act. This is option B
